deliverable: D5 — the pending/early-view boundary and the radar's real status
status_of_the_radar: M9.4's Early Radar exists, is tested, and has no production constructor: it is not wired into the run link, so no end-to-end radar claim is made and none is verified (§7's exact instruction)
what_this_proves: no crate outside crates/live names the radar's vocabulary in code, and the same needles are reported 78 times inside crates/live/src — so the zeros are the boundary, not dead needles
the four calls that would put a radar on a socket occur 17 times, all of them in test code, and 0 times in code a binary builds
the run loop's `MarketEvent::Candidate` arm writes the candidates evidence file and reaches neither the engine, the dispatch, a simulation, nor a send; the sibling `Canonical` arm reaches all of them
the three pending *block* reads exist and are used by the candidate source, while the four crates that own signing, submission, simulation and the run loop call none of them
the only pending read the execution lane makes is `eth_getTransactionCount(address, "pending")` for the nonce, and it is named as one
evm-execution and evm-live have no production dependency edge in either direction, while evm-pipeline legitimately holds both
what_this_does_not_prove: it does not claim the radar works end-to-end: its only real-endpoint harness, crates/live/tests/preconf_live_giwa.rs, is #[ignore]d and was not run (§9 forbids contacting a real endpoint)

it does not re-verify the pending response shapes — that is M12-B's gate, crates/live/tests/pending_shape_compat.rs, which `cargo test --workspace` runs; this file only states where a parsed pending value may then go

it does not re-verify what crates/live/tests/preconf_isolation.rs already proves (the radar's type names absent from the discovery-side crates, and no build path from evm-live to a canonical writer); this file scans the opposite direction, from the signer outward, which that gate does not walk
no new RPC method, no node, no signature, no broadcast: the five tests are std-only text scans over this repository
